summary: PBDB holds first and last appearance ages per genus, an environment field per collection to separate marine from terrestrial settings, and collection and occurrence counts for sampling standardization. Its ages are stage-level in the records seen, so 'one after another' can only be resolved at that grain. Neotoma covers only the late Cenozoic; two Dryad deposits give terrestrial-tetrapod and PBDB/OBIS occurrence extracts.
next_step: Pre-register marine and terrestrial genus first-appearance extractions from PBDB (environment mapping, stage bins, sampling-standardized counts) and a clustering criterion for 'simultaneous batches' at that resolution.
obstacles_confirmed: Stage-level binning limits resolution of simultaneity.
PBDB envtype=terr is not a valid filter value; environment must be mapped from the env field.
Terrestrial record is much thinner than marine in the counts I could obtain (not quantified).
